items.title: Australian couple trapped in Argentina with no legal rights to biological child
items.description: Jonathan and Amy had a child via surrogacy in Argentina. They have been stuck there for 12 months, unable to bring their daughter home.

items.title: Breaking: SA secures Australian MotoGP, world-first street circuit announced
items.description: The South Australian government has confirmed the Australian MotoGP will move to Adelaide from 2027.

items.title: Could Australia permanently ban the 'ISIS brides' from coming home?
items.description: One of the Australian women being held in a Syrian refugee camp has been barred from returning home after being given a temporary exclusion order — but the ban may not be as temporary as the name implies.

items.title: Live: PM says he 'has nothing but contempt' for women in Syria with links to ISIS
items.description: The prime minister says he has "nothing but contempt" for Australian women who travelled to Syria to join ISIS. Follow live.

items.title: Breaking: Unemployment rate remains at 4.1 pc in January
items.description: Australia's unemployment rate remained at 4.1 pc in January, with 17,800 more employed people.

items.title: As solar booms, an Australian technology is rolled out around the world
items.description: At the interface of AI, big data, the energy transition and mind-bogglingly complex weather systems, the ongoing supply of electricity relies on answering a deceptively simple question: Will it be sunny?

items.title: Climate disinformation, the Atlas Network and Dr Karl
items.description: The scourge of AI-slopaganda, viral disinformation campaigns and online attacks against individuals and institutions is going to get far worse before it gets better, if the latest public hearings on the topic are any indication.

items.title: Australia's largest mosque demands security boost over threatening letters
items.description: Another threatening letter has been sent to Lakemba Mosque in Sydney's west, the third in recent weeks just hours before the start of Ramadan on Wednesday.

items.title: Ukraine recaptures territory amid 'extraordinary' Russian casualties
items.description: Ukraine has made its largest battlefield gains in more than two and a half years, retaking more than 200 square kilometres of its territory from Russia in just five days, according to a new analysis.

items.title: Zuckerberg says Meta no longer designs apps to maximise screen time
items.description: The Meta chief executive's comments were made in a landmark trial over youth social media addiction.

items.title: Dani Scott's tears of joy a welcome balm after years of pain
items.description: In this most tension-filled Winter Olympic sport, it's no wonder tears are a by-product of both success and failure. Thankfully for Dani Scott, this time she was crying tears of pure joy.

items.title: Documents reveal messages between Chinese official and accused spy trio
items.description: The police case relies on WeChat communication allegedly between the trio in Australia and a person at China's Public Security Bureau.

items.title: Bar declared crime scene as ACT police seize 'clearly satirical' posters under new hate laws
items.description: Police have seized five posters on display in the window of a Canberra bar, declaring a "crime scene" while they investigate the artworks under new Commonwealth hate laws.

items.title: Darwin public servant charged over alleged $5m NDIS fraud
items.description: A 47-year-old Darwin public servant has been arrested and charged for allegedly defrauding $5 million from the National Disability Insurance Scheme.

items.title: Live: ASX follows Wall Street higher, unemployment steady
items.description: While the unemployment rate remains steady, the ASX opened strongly on the back of a batch of solid results. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: From crime heists to a BDSM love story, here's what's in cinemas this month
items.description: Australians will also finally be able to catch Sirât and The Voice of Hind Rajab, two movies that will be vying for Best International Film at the Academy Awards next month.

items.title: Woman finds Antarctic pioneer's unmarked grave in Melbourne
items.description: Captain John King Davis was one of Australia's greatest Antarctic explorers, but for decades, his final resting place was an unmarked grave in Melbourne. Today, that will change.

items.title: Australia set for highest government debt levels since World War II
items.description: Australia will cease to be a low-debt country and be more vulnerable in a future crisis without a combination of spending restraint and tax reform, a new report has warned.

items.title: 'Blatant' fake discounting by retailers in ACCC's sights
items.description: ACCC chair Gina Cass-Gottlieb outlines the consumer watchdog's priorities for 2026, including targeting "blatant" fake discounting.

items.title: As Sisonke held what police say was an IED, she waited for them to act
items.description: When Sisonke picked up a device that looked like a glass jar in Perth on Australia Day, she had a sense of foreboding so she took it to police. She says they took some time to act.

items.title: Nine reporter says she 'shouldn't have had a drink' before viral live cross
items.description: Danika Mason has apologised for letting her standards slip during a live cross to the Today show from the Winter Olympics in Milano Cortina.

items.title: Trump official says US did not censor Colbert interview but is probing The View
items.description: The confirmation of a probe into the daytime talk show came after it interviewed the same Democratic candidate whose interview with Stephen Colbert was allegedly barred from airing.

items.title: More women are playing footy than ever before. Why are so many leaving?
items.description: The women's team from Kyneton's 15-month public and bitter saga suggests it is the canary in the coal mine of a widespread issue for women's players across the country.

items.title: Trainspotting: How Britpop and beats shaped an era-defining soundtrack
items.description: Most films are lucky to get just one needle-drop moment embedded in the Zeitgeist. Trainspotting boasted several.

items.title: Eight back-country skiers found dead, one missing after avalanche in California
items.description: Eight skiers have been found dead and one is missing after an avalanche in California, making it the deadliest avalanche in the US in forty years.
